cands.name: Pebblin W. Warren

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Alabama House District 82 since 2005. Her professional background includes serving as director of student services for the Alabama Department of Postsecondary Education. She holds bachelor's and graduate degrees from Tuskegee University.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended by the Sway voting groups Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy for 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to Alabama. We found no sponsored-bill details, no policy statements, and nothing on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table was empty in the copy we read.

qual.background: Alabama House member for District 82 since 2005 (21 years), serving on the Ways and Means General Fund Committee. Worked as director of student services at the Alabama Department of Postsecondary Education.
qual.why: More than two decades of prior legislative service, including a seat on the committee that handles the state General Fund budget, plus a state-agency career. Committee membership itself adds nothing to the score; the score rests on the years in office.

cands.name: Kinsley Hammons
cands.bio: Small business owner from Auburn, Alabama, and owner of Hammons Hardscapes. Holds an associate's degree from Southern Union State Community College. Member of the Auburn Chamber of Commerce and Kiwanis Club. Republican candidate for Alabama House District 82 in 2026. Has held no prior public office.
cands.gaps: We found no birthplace, hometown or date he moved to Alabama. We found no public record of his stance on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, campaign money pledges, policing, guns or abortion. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His campaign site gives only general statements on jobs, small business, education, healthcare, agriculture and term limits. We found no news coverage of him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he will support public schools and teachers and career pathways for students. It names no voucher, charter or choice position and no teacher pay figure, so the match to the plank is partial.
